sites.n: Old quarters of Sinaw (Harat Al Barashid and Harat as-Sawafah)
sites.s: About 300-year-old mud-and-stone quarters beside Sinaw’s famous souq
sites.dr: Quarters about 300 years old (2022); documented in a 2014 heritage management plan
sites.el: Two neighbouring harats in one master plan
sites.te: The town of the desert market
sites.se: Beside the market where Bedouin and fishermen trade, old houses with carved doors stand in the Sinaw oasis
sites.sa: بجوار السوق الذي يلتقي فيه البدو والصيادون تقف بيوت قديمة بأبواب منقوشة في واحة سناو
sites.desc: Harat Al Barashid and Harat as-Sawafah are neighbouring old quarters in the Sinaw oasis, Ash Sharqiyah North, documented by ArCHIAM for the Ministry of Heritage and Culture after a survey in autumn 2013, with a joint heritage management plan completed in 2014. Sinaw’s old quarters, described in 2022 as about 300 years old, contain mosques, traditional souqs, Qur’an schools and castles with high round towers, built of stone and clay with massive columns, decorated doors and arches. The traditional souq has four gates and remains a trading place where Bedouin and coastal fishermen sell their products. Many roofs have collapsed and the quarters are largely abandoned.
sites.sig: Historic quarters of one of the main market towns between the Hajar mountains and the Sharqiyah desert.

sites.s: Tidal inlet near Al Kahil with flamingos and wintering shorebirds · Key Biodiversity Area
sites.se: On the Al Wusta coast, a long tidal lagoon fills with flamingos, spoonbills and thousands of sandpipers in winter
sites.sa: على ساحل الوسطى تمتلئ بحيرة مدّ طويلة في الشتاء بطيور النحام وأبي ملعقة وآلاف الطيور الخواضة
sites.desc: A tidal inlet about 6 km long near the township of Al Kahil on the Al Wusta coast, recognised as a Key Biodiversity Area covering about 6.07 km². Counts include 3,000 curlew sandpipers (Calidris ferruginea) in December, 1,500 greater flamingos in November, up to 110 Eurasian spoonbills, 234 ruddy turnstones, 104 pied avocets and 21 ospreys in February. The site lies within the proposed South Jazir National Nature Reserve of 18,000 ha. The Ministry of Heritage and Tourism describes it as a tidal lagoon with white dunes about 6 km east of Al Kahil.
sites.sig: A key wintering and passage wetland for waterbirds on Oman’s central Arabian Sea coast.

sites.s: Mudflats and bay at Duqm with 3,000 flamingos and 77 bird species · Key Biodiversity Area
sites.dr: Key Biodiversity Area (criteria A1b, D1a); last assessed 1994
sites.te: Flamingos at the new port town
sites.ta: طيور النحام في مدينة الميناء الجديدة
sites.se: Beside the fast-growing port of Duqm, a sandy bay and mudflats feed thousands of flamingos every winter
sites.sa: بجوار ميناء الدقم المتنامي يقدّم خليج رملي ومسطحات طينية الغذاء لآلاف طيور النحام كل شتاء
sites.desc: A coastal Key Biodiversity Area of about 14.31 km² near the town of Ad Duqm on the bay of Ghubbat Quwayrat, Al Wusta. A total of 77 bird species has been recorded, with wintering counts of 3,000 greater flamingos, 212 Eurasian spoonbills in February, 175 pied avocets, 31 ospreys and 30 great egrets. It qualifies under global KBA criteria A1b and D1a, but only about 5% of the area is protected. The Ministry of Heritage and Tourism notes that the muddy flats beside Duqm’s 5-km beach attract sandpipers, plovers, avocets and greater flamingos.
sites.sig: An important waterbird site now beside one of Oman’s largest development zones.

sites.s: Ediacaran stromatolite reefs and lagoons of the Huqf · recovery after the Shuram excursion
sites.dr: Buah Formation, Nafun Group (about 645–547 Ma), Huqf Supergroup
sites.el: Section BD1 spans 106.6 m of strata
sites.se: In the Huqf desert, rocks more than 550 million years old preserve reefs and lagoons built by microbial mats
sites.sa: في صحراء الحقف تحفظ صخور يزيد عمرها على 550 مليون عام شعابًا وبحيرات ضحلة بنتها حصائر ميكروبية
sites.desc: Buah Dome in the Huqf area exposes the Buah Formation, a late Precambrian carbonate platform of the Nafun Group (about 645–547 Ma) in the Huqf Supergroup. Bergmann (2013) logged sections BD1–BD4 here and at nearby Mukhaibah Dome, describing reef facies of large domal and columnar stromatolites, Conophyton stromatolites in lagoons, oolitic shoals and evaporite pseudomorphs in peritidal beds. Carbon isotopes, which fall to about −12‰ in the underlying Shuram Formation, recover through the Buah from about −8‰ to about 0‰ and above. A positive excursion in the upper Buah is correlated with the Nama Group dated at 548.8 ± 1 Ma.
sites.sig: A reference platform for how the carbon cycle recovered after the Shuram excursion, just before the first skeletal animals of the Ara Group.
refs: Bergmann, K.D. (2013). Constraints on the Carbon Cycle and Climate During the Early Evolution of Animals. PhD thesis, California Institute of Technology. Chapter 5 and Appendix C. https://doi.org/10.7907/KFJX-7S28
sites.conf: Coordinates are the base of section BD1 in Bergmann (2013), Table C.1; timeline is an estimate within the 645–547 Ma Nafun Group range for the post-Shuram Buah interval, not a direct date; Arabic spelling of Buah is a transliteration. About 37 km from the existing Wadi Shuram point

sites.s: Portuguese harbour fort of Old Muscat · later Oman's main prison, now a museum
sites.el: Prison held about 200 inmates at times
sites.te: The fortress at the harbour gate
sites.se: High on the rocks of Old Muscat, this Portuguese fort guarded the harbour, became a prison and is now a museum
sites.sa: فوق صخور مسقط القديمة يقف هذا الحصن البرتغالي الذي حرس الميناء، ثم صار سجنًا، وهو اليوم متحف
sites.desc: Al Jalali stands on the eastern side of Muscat harbour, facing Al Mirani across the bay. The Portuguese sent Captain Belchior Calaça in 1587 to build it on an earlier Omani site, and it was completed with Al Mirani between 1586 and 1588 as Forte de São João. Persian forces captured the forts in 1738 and again in 1743. For much of the 20th century it was Oman's main prison, holding about 200 prisoners at times, until it closed in the 1970s; it was restored in 1983 as a museum of Omani cultural history.
sites.sig: One of the twin forts that defined Muscat's harbour defences from the Portuguese period to the Al Bu Said state.

sites.s: Portuguese fort on the west side of Muscat harbour · reopened to visitors in 2025
sites.dr: Built by the Portuguese in 1587 on an earlier fortress
sites.te: The fort that watched the Portuguese leave
sites.se: Across the bay from Al Jalali, Al Mirani guarded Muscat until Omani forces took the city from the Portuguese in 1649
sites.sa: في الجهة المقابلة لقلعة الجلالي حرست قلعة الميراني مسقط حتى انتزعها العمانيون من البرتغاليين عام 1649
sites.desc: Al Mirani was built by the Portuguese in 1587 on top of an earlier fortress, on the west side of Muscat harbour opposite Al Jalali. With Al Jalali it was meant to guard the port against Ottoman advances; in 1623 it was the more important of the two and served as the governor's summer residence. Omani forces under Sultan bin Saif took Muscat in 1649, and the Portuguese who fled into the fort surrendered in January 1650. Ahmad bin Said al-Busaidi took control of it in 1749; it later served as a military post and prison, and reopened to the public in April 2025.
sites.sig: A key witness to the end of Portuguese rule in Oman and the rise of the Ya'ariba and Al Bu Said states.
disc: Taken by Ahmad bin Said in 1749

sites.s: Watchtower fort above Muttrah harbour · Portuguese towers turned Ya'ariba fort
sites.dr: Towers possibly 1507; present form early Ya'ariba period (1624–1742)
sites.se: Two old watchtowers on a ridge above Muttrah grew into a fort that guarded the trading harbour
sites.sa: برجان قديمان للمراقبة على مرتفع فوق مطرح تحوّلا إلى قلعة تحرس الميناء التجاري
sites.desc: Muttrah Fort crowns a ridge overlooking the harbour and coastal settlement of Muttrah. Its watchtowers may date to 1507 and were probably modified by the Portuguese in the late 16th century. The Ya'ariba (1624–1742) likely turned them into a proper fort early in their rule over Muscat and Muttrah. The Royal Oman Police used it in the late 20th century, and in 2018 it opened to visitors as a venue for arts and cultural events.
sites.sig: Shows how Muscat's twin harbours were defended from the Portuguese era into the Ya'ariba period.
refs: Archnet. Matrah Fort. https://www.archnet.org/sites/22207 (accessed 9 November 2026)
Peterson, J.E. (2007). Historical Muscat: An Illustrated Guide and Gazetteer. Leiden: Brill.

sites.s: Inland fort guarding Old Muscat's water supply · named for irrigation
sites.dr: Built mid-17th century; restored in the 1970s
sites.el: About 1 km inland from Old Muscat
sites.te: The fort that guarded the water
sites.se: In Wadi al-Kabir behind Old Muscat, this small fort protected the wells and gardens that kept the city alive
sites.sa: في الوادي الكبير خلف مسقط القديمة حمى هذا الحصن الصغير الآبار والبساتين التي كانت تمد المدينة بالحياة
sites.desc: Fort al-Rawiyah (Qal'at al-Rawiyah) stands in the Tuyan quarter, about 1 km inland along al-Wadi al-Kabir from Old Muscat. It was built in the mid-17th century, attributed to the Portuguese, to protect Muscat's water supply during the advance of Imam Sultan bin Saif al-Ya'rubi; its name refers to irrigation. It was originally three storeys high, with gardens, a cistern and a well. Sultan bin Ahmad renovated it, and the Ministry of National Heritage and Culture restored it in the 1970s; it now stands two storeys high amid modern housing.
sites.sig: A rare surviving link between Muscat's defences and its water supply.
disc: About 1 km inland from Old Muscat

sites.s: Coastal outcrop of eclogite · Arabian margin rocks subducted beneath the Samail Ophiolite
sites.dr: Peak garnet growth c. 81–77 Ma; Permian protolith 283.8 ± 0.7 Ma
sites.te: Rocks that went down and came back
sites.ta: صخور غاصت في الأعماق ثم عادت
sites.se: On the beach north of As Sifah lie rare eclogites, pieces of Arabia pushed deep under the ocean crust and brought back to the surface
sites.sa: على الشاطئ شمال السيفة تنكشف صخور إكلوجيت نادرة، وهي قطع من حافة الجزيرة العربية دُفعت عميقًا تحت القشرة المحيطية ثم عادت إلى السطح
sites.desc: The As Sifah eclogites crop out on the coast about 1–2 km north of As Sifah village, in the north-east of the Saih Hatat window. They are the structurally lowest, highest-grade rocks beneath the Samail Ophiolite and record continental-margin rocks subducted to peak conditions of about 2.0–2.5 GPa and 550 °C. Zircon cores show a Permian volcanic protolith (283.8 ± 0.7 Ma). Garnet, zircon and rutile dates (about 80.9 to 75.9 Ma) show garnet growth from about 81 to 77 Ma, during subduction beneath the ophiolite.
sites.sig: A key natural laboratory for dating continental subduction and exhumation beneath the Samail Ophiolite.
refs: Garber, J.M., Rioux, M., Searle, M.P., Kylander-Clark, A.R.C., Hacker, B.R., Vervoort, J.D., Warren, C.J. & Smye, A.J. (2021). Dating continental subduction beneath the Samail Ophiolite: garnet, zircon, and rutile petrochronology of the As Sifah eclogites, NE Oman. Journal of Geophysical Research: Solid Earth 126, e2021JB022715. https://doi.org/10.1029/2021JB022715
sites.conf: Coordinates are sample CWO237 (23°27'30"N, 58°46'48"E) from Garber et al. (2021); the outcrop extends a few hundred metres. Timeline spans the dated metamorphic growth (≈81 to 75.9 Ma).

sites.s: Fishing village reachable only by sea · home of the Kumzari language
sites.te: The village at the end of the sea road
sites.ta: القرية التي لا يصلها إلا البحر
sites.se: Hidden in a cove near the tip of Musandam, Kumzar can only be reached by boat and keeps its own language
sites.sa: في خليج صغير قرب رأس مسندم تختبئ كمزار، فلا يصلها أحد إلا بالقارب، وما زال أهلها يتحدثون لغتهم الخاصة
sites.desc: Kumzar is a fishing village near the northern tip of the Musandam Peninsula, accessible only by boat, with no road to Khasab. It has been inhabited for about 500 years, and early Portuguese maps show a settlement in the area. Its people speak Kumzari, a Southwestern Iranian language influenced by up to 45 languages including Arabic. Many families keep a second house in Khasab and leave Kumzar from May to September because of the summer heat.
sites.sig: A living example of isolated maritime settlement and linguistic heritage at the Strait of Hormuz.

sites.s: Bronze and Iron Age collective tombs · at least 188 people and thousands of objects
sites.dr: c. 2000–600 BC (LCG-1 mainly Iron Age I–II)
sites.se: Found by chance in 2012 in Dibba, long stone tombs held the remains of nearly 200 people with bronze, soft-stone vessels and beads
sites.sa: اكتُشفت مصادفة عام 2012 في دبا مقابر حجرية طويلة ضمّت رفات نحو 200 شخص مع أوانٍ برونزية وحجرية وخرز
sites.desc: The site lies on the east coast of the Musandam Peninsula at Dibba al-Bayah, overlooking the Gulf of Oman, and was found by accident in 2012 during infrastructure works. Long Collective Grave 1 (LCG-1), about 14 × 3.5 m and lined with limestone blocks, held at least 188 individuals (153 adults and 35 subadults) in secondary deposition. It yielded 9,666 items, with 1,730 more in five external pits, including 241 soft-stone vessels; a second tomb, LCG-2 (23 × 6 m), produced more than 3,000 objects. Use spans the Wadi Suq period (c. 2000–1600 BC) to Iron Age II, with most material from Iron Age I–II.
sites.sig: One of the richest Bronze–Iron Age funerary deposits in south-east Arabia, studied by an Italian–Omani mission since 2013.
refs: Genchi, F. & Tursi, G. (2022). The softstone vessels assemblage from the Long Collective Grave 1 (LCG-1) at Dibbā al-Bayah (Sultanate of Oman): a preliminary assessment. Arabian Archaeology and Epigraphy. https://doi.org/10.1111/aae.12209

sites.s: High plateau below Jabal Harim · hotspot of new plant records for Oman
sites.te: A mountain garden of rare plants
sites.se: High on Musandam's mountains, the As Sayh plateau and Jabal Harim slopes hold plants found nowhere else in Oman
sites.sa: في أعالي جبال مسندم تحتضن هضبة السيح ومنحدرات جبل الحارم نباتات لا توجد في أي مكان آخر من عُمان
sites.desc: As Sayh is a high plateau with old cultivation terraces beneath Jabal Harim, Musandam's highest mountain. A 2020 botanical study reported 60 new or extended plant records for Oman, about one-third of them (21 species) from Musandam, mostly between about 1,135 and 1,620 m on the As Sayh and As Sahosa slopes of Jabal Harim. Records include Piptatherum holciforme on the Sayh plateau at 1,136 m and Vicia monantha at 1,135 m, while Medicago coronata, new for Arabia, was found on disused terraces at 530 m on the Khasab–Jabal Harim road.
sites.sig: Shows that Musandam's cool uplands hold a distinct, Irano-Turanian-influenced flora still being discovered.
refs: Patzelt, A., Al Hatmi, S., Al Hinai, A., Al Qassabi, Z. & Knees, S.G. (2020). Studies in the flora of Arabia: XXXIV. Sixty new records from the Sultanate of Oman. Edinburgh Journal of Botany 77(3), 413–437. https://doi.org/10.1017/S0960428620000086
sites.conf: Coordinates are the Piptatherum holciforme voucher on the Sayh plateau (25°59'32.3"N, 56°12'51.6"E) in Patzelt et al. (2020). About 2.5 km from the existing Jabal Al Harim geosite, but this record covers the plateau flora. No formal designation; t0 uses the 2020 publication.

sites.na: أفران صهر النحاس في وادي الخطوة
sites.s: Chain of ancient copper smelters along a mountain gorge · copper carried to the Sohar coast
sites.p: Undated (regional smelting from the Bronze Age to early Islamic times)
sites.dr: Not dated; regional smelting periods from the 3rd or 2nd millennium BC to shortly after the arrival of Islam
sites.se: Along the gorges of Wadi Khutwah, clay furnaces and heaps of slag show where people once turned rock into copper
sites.sa: على امتداد شعاب وادي الخطوة تكشف بقايا أفران طينية وأكوام خبث أين حوّل الناس الصخر إلى نحاس
sites.desc: Six copper smelting sites (SM1–SM6) lie on both sides of the gorges of Wadi Khutwah, in the foothills of the Hajar Mountains, with a suspected ore-roasting pit upstream near Sultan's Oasis. Each smelter was built a short distance from a falaj or stream and needed clay for bricks, which often bear the makers' finger impressions, plus large amounts of charcoal and ore. SM6 has more slag cores than any other Khutwah smelter, with debris more than a metre deep in places, suggesting several smelting seasons. The copper was probably cast into small ingots and carried by donkey or camel to the Sohar coast.
sites.sig: A compact, well-mapped example of the small-scale copper industry that made the Oman mountains famous as ancient Magan.
sites.ex: ENHG; Experience Oman Al Buraimi guide
disc: Debris over 1 m deep at SM6

sites.s: Square Sasanian fort in the Sohar hinterland · the only securely dated Late Sasanian fort in Arabia
sites.dr: Built early 5th to mid-6th century AD; used into the 7th century
sites.el: 30 × 30 m with walls about 2.65 m thick
sites.te: A Persian fort on the Batinah
sites.se: Thirteen kilometres inland from the sea near Saham, a square stone fort shows that the Sasanian Persians held this coast before Islam
sites.sa: على بعد 13.5 كيلومترًا من البحر قرب صحم يكشف حصن حجري مربع أن الساسانيين سيطروا على هذا الساحل قبل الإسلام
sites.desc: Fulayj lies on the Batinah plain about 30 km south of Sohar and about 13.5 km inland, near Falaj al-Harth, and was found in the 2012 Saham survey. The fort is square, 30 × 30 m, with walls about 2.65 m thick of unshaped stone and lime mortar, four solid U-shaped corner towers and a single 1.62 m-wide eastern entrance. Thirteen AMS dates place construction and main occupation in the early 5th to mid-6th century AD, including a lime kiln dated to about 415–560 AD, with later use about 625–681 AD. Excavations yielded 2,313 sherds.
sites.sig: Direct evidence of Sasanian military control of the Omani coast before the Islamisation of south-east Arabia.
refs: Al-Jahwari, N.S., Kennet, D., Priestman, S. & Sauer, E. (2018). Fulayj: a Late Sasanian fort on the Arabian coast. Antiquity 92(363), 724–741. https://doi.org/10.15184/aqy.2018.64

sites.s: Two tidal inlets with extensive mangroves · Key Biodiversity Area for gulls and kingfishers
sites.dr: Key Biodiversity Area (legacy IBA), last assessed 1994
sites.te: The mangrove creeks of Shinas and Liwa
sites.se: Two tidal creeks on the northern Batinah coast are lined with mangroves where rare kingfishers and big gulls gather
sites.sa: خوران على ساحل الباطنة الشمالي تحفّهما أشجار القرم، تجتمع فيهما طيور الرفراف النادرة والنوارس الكبيرة
sites.desc: Khawr Shinas and Khawr Liwa are two tidal inlets on the northern Batinah coast supporting extensive Avicennia mangrove, together covering about 29.1 km² at 0–5 m altitude. A total of 118 bird species has been recorded, with up to 103 roosting Pallas's gulls (Larus ichthyaetus) in winter. The endangered collared kingfisher subspecies Todirhamphus chloris kalbaensis occurs irregularly in the mangrove, and Sykes's warbler (Hippolais rama) probably breeds. Two nature reserves have been proposed, Khawr Shinas (2,100 ha) and Khawr Nabr (2,300 ha), but none is yet established.
sites.sig: Among the largest mangrove creeks of Oman's Batinah coast and a refuge for a mangrove-dependent kingfisher.

sites.s: About 300 km of sandy beach and creek mouths · wintering waders, gulls and terns
sites.dr: Key Biodiversity Area (legacy IBA), last assessed 1994
sites.te: The long beach of the shorebirds
sites.se: From Seeb to Shinas, Oman's longest sandy beach is a winter home for sanderlings, gulls and terns
sites.sa: من السيب إلى شناص يمتد أطول شاطئ رملي في عُمان، وهو مشتى لطيور الشاطئ المهاجرة والنوارس وخطاف البحر
sites.desc: The Al Batinah coast Key Biodiversity Area covers about 300 km of exposed sandy beach facing the Gulf of Oman, from As Seeb north-west to Shinas, totalling about 59.1 km² at 0–5 m. Khawrs form at the mouths of drainage lines, though most are transitory; five major khawrs (Kalba, Shinas, Liwa, Ra's/Juzor as Sawadi and Al Qurm) are assessed as separate sites. Sanderling (Calidris alba) occurs in important numbers in winter, along with roosting gulls and terns. Seven Nature Conservation Areas totalling 860 ha have been proposed along the coast.
sites.sig: The main sandy-shore habitat for wintering shorebirds on Oman's most populated coast.
refs: KBA Partnership. Al Batinah coast (KBA 8220). World Database of Key Biodiversity Areas. https://www.keybiodiversityareas.org/site/factsheet/8220 (accessed 9 November 2026)

sites.s: Fort built over a rock outcrop at the foot of Jebel Nakhal · pre-Islamic origins, 1834 towers
sites.dr: Pre-Islamic origins; rebuilt 17th century; extended 1834; restored 1990
sites.el: Six towers on a rocky outcrop
sites.te: The fort that grew out of the rock
sites.se: Nakhal Fort rises straight out of a rocky hill, its walls wrapped around the natural stone above the palm groves
sites.sa: ترتفع قلعة نخل مباشرة من تل صخري، وتلتف جدرانها حول الحجر الطبيعي فوق بساتين النخيل
sites.desc: Nakhal Fort sits on a rocky prominence at the foot of Jebel Nakhal, overlooking palm groves and the route to the Ain al-Thawarah spring, about 120 km west of Muscat. Its origins are believed to be pre-Islamic, and it was rebuilt in the 17th century under the Bani Kharous and Ya'ariba imams. The gateway and towers seen today were extensions of 1834 attributed to Said bin Sultan. Six towers encircle the two-storey fort, which incorporates the natural rock into its structure; the last major restoration was in 1990.
sites.sig: A classic example of an Omani fort shaped by and built into its rock foundation.
refs: Ministry of Heritage and Tourism, Oman. Nakhl Fort. https://experienceoman.om/destinations/al-batinah-south/nakhl-fort (accessed 9 November 2026)
Wikipedia contributors. Nakhal Fort. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nakhal_Fort (accessed 9 November 2026)

sites.s: Fortress-palace of Imam Sultan bin Saif II · stone vaults with no wood
sites.el: Ceilings of stone vaults, with no timber
sites.se: Built in 1708 for an imam, Al Hazm has stone-vaulted ceilings, secret passages and old Portuguese and Spanish cannons
sites.sa: بُنيت قلعة الحزم عام 1708 لإمام عُماني، وفيها أسقف حجرية مقببة وممرات سرية ومدافع برتغالية وإسبانية قديمة
sites.desc: Al Hazm Castle stands on flat land beside Wadi Rustaq in Al Batinah South. It was built in 1120 AH / 1708 AD by Imam Sultan bin Saif II as his residence, and he was buried within it after his death in 1718. The square castle has two towers reached by stairways designed for horses, two gateways, and ceilings carried on stone arches without wood. It houses Portuguese and Spanish cannons, tunnels and secret passages, and rooms once used for teaching the Qur'an and sciences; it was restored in 1996.
sites.sig: A late Ya'ariba fortress-palace that shows the peak of Omani defensive architecture.
refs: Ministry of Heritage and Tourism, Oman. Al Hazm Castle. https://experienceoman.om/destinations/al-batinah-south/al-hazm-castle (accessed 9 November 2026)

sites.na: موقع التيخة من فترة أم النار
sites.s: Large Early Bronze Age settlement with round towers near Rustaq
sites.el: About 50 ha, 35 ha with Umm an-Nar occupation
sites.te: A Bronze Age village of towers
sites.se: On a terrace of Wadi Far near Rustaq, people of the Umm an-Nar age built round towers, houses and stone tombs
sites.sa: على مصطبة في وادي الفرع قرب الرستاق بنى أهل فترة أم النار أبراجًا دائرية وبيوتًا ومقابر حجرية
sites.desc: Al-Tikha lies about 5 km north of old Rustaq on a Quaternary alluvial terrace on the west bank of Wadi Far, just south of its confluence with Wadi Sahtan. The site covers about 50 ha, with about 35 ha of Umm an-Nar occupation, including three certain round towers. Occupation area S1 has about 20 stone structures on roughly 1 ha, and S2 is a courtyard complex of about 1,000 m². The cemetery has at least four tombs and is tentatively dated from 2700–2600 BC, reaching its greatest extent in 2600–2200 BC; a transect survey collected about 3,500 sherds.
sites.sig: One of the largest documented Umm an-Nar settlements on the Batinah side of the Hajar Mountains, informing how third-millennium communities lived.
refs: Deadman, W.M., Kennet, D., de Vreeze, M. & al-Jahwari, N.S. (2022). The nature of third-millennium settlement: the example of al-Tikha (Rustaq), an Umm an-Nar site on the Batinah coast of Oman. Arabian Archaeology and Epigraphy 33, 49–84. https://doi.org/10.1111/aae.12218
sites.conf: Coordinates converted from UTM 40N ≈544200 E, 2592100 N (WGS 84) printed in Deadman et al. (2022; northing misprinted there as 25921001), ≈100 m. Chronology is described by the authors as tentative. Arabic name is a careful transliteration.

sites.n: Ra's as Sawadi and Juzor as Sawadi
sites.s: Headland, khawr and eight islands · breeding herons, ospreys and sooty falcons
sites.dr: Key Biodiversity Area (legacy IBA), last assessed 1994; proposed National Scenic Reserve
sites.el: About 10.1 km²; c. 25 pairs of Western Reef Heron
sites.te: The islands of the reef herons
sites.se: Off the Sawadi headland, eight small islands shelter nesting herons, ospreys and sooty falcons above coral reefs
sites.sa: قبالة رأس السوادي تأوي ثماني جزر صغيرة أعشاش البلشون والعقاب النساري وصقر الغروب فوق شعاب مرجانية
sites.desc: Ra's as Sawadi is a headland north-west of As Seeb with a khawr, beach, sandbars and eight offshore islands, covering about 10.1 km² at 0–30 m. About 25 pairs of Western Reef Heron (Egretta gularis) and at least two pairs of Osprey (Pandion haliaetus) breed on the islands, which are also an important breeding site for Sooty Falcon (Falco concolor). Extensive mudflats in the khawr hold wintering and passage waterbirds, and high-quality coral reefs surround the islands. The two largest islands hold settlement sites more than 4,000 years old.
sites.sig: A compact mix of seabird islands, coral and mudflat on the Batinah coast, still only proposed for protection.
refs: KBA Partnership. Ra's as Sawadi - Juzor as Sawadi (KBA 8222). World Database of Key Biodiversity Areas. https://www.keybiodiversityareas.org/site/factsheet/8222 (accessed 9 November 2026)

sites.s: Walled clifftop quarter guarding Ibri oasis · towers, souq and falaj
sites.dr: More than 600 years old (visitor guide); documented 2012–2013
sites.el: Seven towers on a rocky cliff
sites.te: The fortress village on the cliff
sites.se: On a rocky cliff at the edge of Ibri oasis, the walled mud-brick town of Al Sulaif has towers, a souq and a falaj running beneath it
sites.sa: على جرف صخري عند طرف واحة عبري تقف بلدة السليف المسوّرة المبنية من الطين، بأبراجها وسوقها وفلجها الذي يجري تحتها
sites.desc: Harat as-Sulayf is a walled settlement on a rocky cliff at the eastern edge of the Ibri oasis, controlling access to the oasis. Mud-brick buildings on stone foundations, mostly two storeys, line streets running up and down the slope, with a mosque, a souq and access points to an underground falaj. The castle is said to be more than 600 years old and has seven towers and extensive battlements, with Quranic quotations and hand imprints on some arches. The site was documented in 2012–2013 for a heritage management and development plan for the Ministry of Heritage and Culture.
sites.sig: A well-preserved fortified oasis quarter showing how settlements, defence and water were integrated in Ad Dhahirah.
refs: ArCHIAM (2013). Documentation and Heritage Management Plan: Harat as-Sulayf, Ibri Oasis. https://archiam.co.uk/documentation-and-heritage-management-plan-harat-as-sulayf-ibri-oasis (accessed 9 November 2026)
Emirates Natural History Group (2004). Ibri Fort and City, 16 April 2004. https://enhg.org/field/ibri/ibri.htm (accessed 9 November 2026)
Lonely Planet. Sulaif Castle. https://www.lonelyplanet.com/points-of-interest/sulaif-castle/1612820 (accessed 9 November 2026)

sites.s: Late pre-Islamic warrior graves at the foot of Jabal Kawr · swords, arrowheads and bronze bowls
sites.se: Near the village of Amlah, stone-lined graves held iron swords, daggers, 41 arrowheads in one grave, and bronze bowls with figures
sites.sa: قرب قرية عملة، ضمّت قبور مبطّنة بالحجارة سيوفًا وخناجر من الحديد، و41 رأس سهم في قبر واحد، وأوعية برونزية مزيّنة بالرسوم
sites.desc: A late pre-Islamic cemetery about 1 km east of the centre of Amlah and 2 km west of the foot of Jabal Kawr, published at N23°07′ E56°54′. Bank and Yule excavated 25 graves: 18 at al-Fueda, 5 at Qurain ar-Rusa and 2 in Wadi al-Mais. The graves are subterranean dry-stone chambers averaging 1.79 m long and 0.65 m wide, with floors about 1 m below the surface. Finds include 14 complete or lightly damaged pots, soft-stone vessels, four bronze bowls and iron weapons; one young man’s grave held three swords, a dagger and 41 arrowheads. The graves are assigned to phases PIR.A and PIR.B (late 3rd to 1st century BC).
sites.sig: Its Samad-style graves with northern PIR-type goods suggest the late pre-Islamic culture of the north reached further south than once thought.
refs: Bank, C. & Yule, P. (2001). Al-Fueda near Amla, Sultanate of Oman. Proceedings of the Seminar for Arabian Studies 31, 15–22. http://www.jstor.org/stable/41223667
Amlah. Wikipedia. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amlah
sites.conf: Coordinates are the published point N23°07′ E56°54′ (Bank & Yule 2001), minute precision, ≈1–2 km. Timeline converted from the PIR.A–PIR.B centuries. Wikipedia gives 26 graves; the paper’s count of 25 is used. Arabic names الفويدة and عملة are careful transliterations to be checked.

sites.s: Triassic limestone massif of the Oman Exotics · a volcanic eruption caught inside a carbonate platform
sites.te: A reef that met a volcano
sites.se: High above Ibri’s eastern oases, Jabal Kawr is a slab of Triassic sea limestone that once grew in a deep ocean basin, with ash from an ancient eruption inside it
sites.sa: يرتفع جبل الكور فوق واحات عبري الشرقية، وهو كتلة من حجر جيري بحري تعود إلى العصر الترياسي، نمت يومًا في حوض محيطي عميق، وتحتضن رمادًا من ثوران بركاني قديم
sites.desc: Jabal Kawr is a cliff-forming mountain on the eastern border of Ad Dhahirah; GeoNames gives its peak at 2,730 m and the Ministry of Heritage and Tourism about 2,700 m. Its carbonates belong to the Triassic Kawr (Kwar) Group of the Oman Exotics, which also builds Jabal Misht, Misfah and Ghul. Basile and Chauvet describe a phreatomagmatic eruption during the growth of this carbonate platform, which developed within the Hawasina basin; in their section the upper carbonate unit is about 150 m thick. The volcanic unit of the Misfah Formation has been dated Ladinian–Carnian from foraminifera, with a revised Norian to Rhaetian age proposed for its members. The mountain’s valleys feed the oases of Al-Abla and Al-Ain to the north and Nadan and Muwal to the west.
sites.sig: One of the large Triassic exotic limestone blocks of the Oman Mountains, recording volcanism in the Neo-Tethys margin basin.
refs: Basile, C. & Chauvet, F. (2006). Phreatomagmatic eruption during the buildup of a Triassic carbonate platform (Oman Exotics): eruptive style, associated deformations, and implications on CO2 release by volcanism. HAL preprint hal-00116078. https://hal.archives-ouvertes.fr/hal-00116078
GeoNames. Highest mountains in Oman (Jabal Kawr peak). https://www.geonames.org/OM/highest-mountains-in-oman.html
Ministry of Heritage and Tourism (Experience Oman). Ad Dhahirah guide. https://experienceoman.om/media/gi5b5zwi/ad-dhahira-en.pdf
sites.conf: Coordinates are the GeoNames peak point (23.139, 57.014), ≈100 m. GeoNames lists the peak under Ad Dakhiliyah; the Ministry guide describes the mountain as on the eastern border of Al Dhahirah, so the region assignment should be checked. Timeline uses standard Ladinian start (≈242 Ma) and Rhaetian end (≈201 Ma) boundaries, not dates from the source. About 14 km from the existing Jebel Misht point. Arabic name جبل الكور follows common usage.

sites.s: Warm spring flowing from a wadi near Nakhal Fort · feeds the aflaj of the oasis
sites.se: Warm water bubbles out of the wadi near Nakhal Fort all year and runs through palm groves, where small fish nibble visitors’ feet
sites.sa: يتدفق ماء دافئ من الوادي قرب حصن نخل طوال العام، ويجري بين بساتين النخيل حيث تداعب أسماك صغيرة أقدام الزوار
sites.desc: A spring a few kilometres from Nakhal Fort, off the road between Barka and Rustaq in the Western Hajar mountains. Its water is warm rather than hot, despite a name linked to the Arabic word for boiling. The spring forms a stream in the wadi, and the Ministry of Regional Municipalities and Water Resources says hot water flows from the wadi continuously and is channelled into aflaj to irrigate nearby farms. A small rectangular concrete pool holds about 15 people, and a development project was reported as nearly 40% complete in 2023. In northern Oman, hot springs are associated with faults at the contact between Tertiary sediments and the Semail Ophiolite.
sites.sig: A permanent spring that shows how groundwater rising along mountain-front faults sustains Oman’s oases and aflaj.

sites.s: Mountain village of mud-and-stone houses and terraced fields below Jebel Shams
sites.se: High in the Hajar Mountains, Bilad Sayt’s clustered houses sit above green terraces, reached only by four-wheel drive
sites.sa: في أعالي جبال الحجر، تتجمع بيوت بلاد سيت فوق مدرّجات خضراء، ولا يُوصل إليها إلا بسيارات الدفع الرباعي
sites.desc: A mountain village on the north-east slope of the Al Hajar Mountains near Jebel Shams, reached through Wadi Bani Awf and Wadi Al Sahtan from the north-east or from Al Hamra in the south-west. It is accessible only by four-wheel-drive vehicles. Its clustered mud-and-stone houses and terraced fields make it a noted heritage landscape, and the Ministry of Heritage and Tourism lists it among the most picturesque villages of South Al Batinah. Census figures give 2,404 people in 2003, 2,484 in 2010 and 3,567 in 2020.
sites.sig: A living example of traditional Omani mountain agriculture, with terraces and stone houses adapted to steep slopes.
refs: Bilad Sayt. Wikipedia. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bilad_Sayt
Ministry of Heritage and Tourism (Experience Oman). Balad Sayt Village. https://experienceoman.om/destinations/al-batinah-south/balad-sayt-village

sites.n: Wadi Al Khlata (Al Khlata Formation type section)
sites.s: Type section of Oman’s ice-age rocks · glacial deposits and striated pavements of the Haushi–Huqf uplift
sites.dr: Al Khlata Formation, Haushi Group: late Moscovian–Asselian (about 311–294 Ma)
sites.el: About 100 m thick at the type section; over 800 m in the subsurface
sites.se: In the Huqf desert, rocks left by glaciers about 300 million years ago still show boulders and pavements scratched by moving ice
sites.sa: في صحراء الحقف ما زالت صخور خلّفتها الأنهار الجليدية قبل نحو 300 مليون عام تحمل جلاميد وأرضيات صخرية خدشها الجليد في أثناء زحفه
sites.desc: Wadi Al Khlata, on the Haushi–Huqf uplift of central Oman, is the type section of the Al Khlata Formation, the glacially influenced base of the Haushi Group, about 100 m thick here. The formation spans the late Moscovian to Asselian (about 311–294 Ma) and consists of diamictites, conglomerates, gravels, pebbly sandstones, siltstones and shales, including laminated shales with dropstones and faceted, striated boulders up to a metre across. Its glacial origin is established by striated pavements cut into the Precambrian Khufai Formation on the western flank of the uplift, whose crag-and-tail features show ice moving towards the north-east. In the subsurface the formation varies from about 100 m to more than 800 m thick and forms hydrocarbon reservoirs.
sites.sig: The reference outcrop for the Late Palaeozoic glaciation of Arabia, when the region lay in southern Gondwana, and a key analogue for Oman’s Al Khlata oil and gas reservoirs.
sites.ex: Stephenson et al. (2013); Middle East Geological Lexicon
refs: Stephenson, M.H., Jan, I.U. & Al-Mashaikie, S.Z.A.K. (2013). Palynology and correlation of Carboniferous–Permian glacigene rocks in Oman, Yemen and Pakistan. Gondwana Research 24(1), 203–211. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.gr.2012.06.005
Middle East Geological Lexicon. Al Khlata Formation (Oman). https://mideastlex.geolex.org/formations/Al%20Khlata%20Fm
sites.conf: Coordinates are the published type-section point 19°46′43″N, 57°25′46″E (Stephenson et al. 2013), second precision; timeline uses the lexicon’s 311.09–293.52 Ma range; Arabic الخلطة is a careful transliteration. About 30 km from Duqm Rock Garden and 38 km from Wadi Shuram

sites.s: Southernmost surface salt dome of central Oman · carries rare fragments of buried basement
sites.dr: Andesite clast dated about 545 Ma (U–Pb zircon); sandstone clast deposited after about 734 Ma
sites.te: A salt elevator from deep below
sites.se: Rising salt at Qarn Sahmah has carried up pieces of volcanic rock from kilometres underground that no one could otherwise reach
sites.sa: رفع الملح الصاعد في قرن سهمة قطعًا من صخور بركانية من أعماق تبلغ كيلومترات، يستحيل الوصول إليها بغير ذلك
sites.desc: Qarn Sahmah is the southernmost of the surface-piercing salt domes of interior central Oman, whose Ara salt carries limestone blocks of the Ara Group up to several hundred metres across. Of the central Oman domes visited by Thomas et al. (2015), only Qarn Sahmah also contains volcanic and sedimentary clasts, concentrated in a small central area; the northern group of five domes holds only Ara Formation clasts. A porphyritic andesite from the dome gave a U–Pb zircon crystallisation age of about 545 Ma, and a red sandstone a maximum depositional age of about 734 Ma. The volcanic samples have ocean-island-basalt-like chemistry with positive Nb–Ta anomalies.
sites.sig: One of very few windows into the hidden Neoproterozoic basement of eastern Arabia, brought to the surface by salt from great depth.
refs: Thomas, R.J., Ellison, R.A., Goodenough, K.M., Roberts, N.M.W. & Allen, P.A. (2015). Salt domes of the UAE and Oman: probing eastern Arabia. Precambrian Research 256, 1–16. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.precamres.2014.10.011
Accepted manuscript: https://nora.nerc.ac.uk/id/eprint/508778/
sites.conf: Coordinates converted from the published sample location of andesite RTOM_9 (457472 E, 2278854 N; Thomas et al. 2015, Table 3), read as UTM zone 40N WGS84 because the paper states no datum or zone; precision ≈ a few hundred metres. Governorate assigned from the coordinate. Arabic قرن سهمة is a careful transliteration. Timeline start is the andesite age; the dome itself is still active

sites.na: مقاطع تكوين الخف عند قبة حوشي
sites.s: Middle Permian sea-floor fossils of the Huqf · the Khuff sea’s edge in central Oman
sites.el: Khuff Formation up to 30–40 m thick
sites.te: Shells of a vanished Permian sea
sites.se: On the flank of the Haushi uplift, marls and limestones are packed with brachiopods and tiny conodonts from a sea that flooded Oman about 265 million years ago
sites.sa: على جانب قبة حوشي تزخر طبقات المارل والحجر الجيري بالعضديات وأحافير الكونودونت الدقيقة من بحر غمر عُمان قبل نحو 265 مليون عام
sites.desc: Five sections along the north-western flank of the Haushi uplift in the Huqf area expose the Khuff Formation, a succession of marine marls and bioclastic limestones up to 30–40 m thick, divided into four members and deposited on an outer shelf. It overlies fluvial rocks of the Gharif Formation and is cut by an angular unconformity beneath the continental Minjur Formation. The beds yield brachiopods (mainly productids, with a mixed fauna dominated by Tethyan genera), conodonts including Hindeodus excavatus and Merrillina praedivergens, foraminifera, bivalves, gastropods, ostracods and cephalopods. Angiolini et al. (1998) assigned the formation here a provisional Wordian (Guadalupian, Middle Permian) age.
sites.sig: Fixes the age of the Khuff marine transgression in south-eastern Oman with fossils, at the edge of the Permian Tethys sea.
refs: Angiolini, L., Nicora, A., Bucher, H., Vachard, D., Pillevuit, A., Platel, J.-P., Roger, J., Baud, A., Broutin, J., Al Hashmi, H. & Marcoux, J. (1998). Evidence of a Guadalupian age for the Khuff Formation of southeastern Oman: preliminary report. Rivista Italiana di Paleontologia e Stratigrafia 104(3), 329–340. https://riviste.unimi.it/index.php/RIPS/article/view/5337

sites.s: Dried-up Late Pleistocene lake in the Omani interior · a possible stepping stone for early humans
sites.el: Lake and river deposits from a humid phase 132,000–104,000 years ago
sites.te: A lake in the middle of the desert
sites.se: Near Saiwan, old lake mud in today’s desert shows that rain once filled a lake here, perhaps helping early humans cross Arabia
sites.sa: قرب سيوان تكشف رواسب بحيرة قديمة وسط الصحراء أن الأمطار ملأت هنا بحيرة يومًا، ولعلها أعانت البشر الأوائل على عبور جزيرة العرب
sites.desc: Near Saiwan in central Oman, relict lake sediments first noted in an earlier reconnaissance were studied by Rosenberg as part of a doctoral project on humid phases recorded in Arabian lake deposits. The fluvial and lacustrine deposits record a short humid period sometime between 132,000 and 104,000 years ago. The area is noted for its rich archaeological evidence, and Rosenberg et al. (2012) proposed the palaeolake as a potential key area for the dispersal of anatomically modern humans out of Africa.
sites.sig: Evidence that the now hyper-arid interior of Oman held a lake between 132,000 and 104,000 years ago, a possible route for modern humans spreading out of Africa.
refs: Rosenberg, T.M., Preusser, F., Blechschmidt, I., Fleitmann, D., Jagher, R. & Matter, A. (2012). Late Pleistocene palaeolake in the interior of Oman: a potential key area for the dispersal of anatomically modern humans out-of-Africa? Journal of Quaternary Science 27(1), 13–16. https://doi.org/10.1002/jqs.1560
Rosenberg, T.M. (2011). Palaeoclimate history of the Arabian Peninsula: humid phases recorded in lake deposits. PhD thesis, University of Bern. https://occrdata.unibe.ch/students/theses/phd/72.pdf
sites.conf: Coordinates are the Oman sample site 20°58′N, 57°22′E given in Rosenberg (2011, ch. 2), minute precision (≈1–2 km); the thesis’s only Oman study area is the palaeolake near Saiwan, but the text does not name the site at that point. Lake size and individual luminescence ages were not available. Arabic سيوان is a careful transliteration; governorate assigned from the coordinate

sites.n: Mudhmar East Iron Age ritual site
sites.na: موقع مضمار الشرقي من العصر الحديدي
sites.s: Iron Age ritual buildings near Adam · bronze weapons, miniatures and snakes
sites.te: The desert shrine of bronze weapons
sites.se: At the foot of Jabal Mudhmar near Adam, a 2,800-year-old building held bronze bows, quivers, daggers and axes, some made too small to use
sites.sa: عند سفح جبل مضمار قرب آدم، ضمّ مبنى عمره نحو 2800 عام أقواسًا وجعابًا وخناجر وفؤوسًا برونزية، صُنع بعضها أصغر من أن يُستعمل
sites.desc: Mudhmar East lies at the eastern tip of Jabal Mudhmar near Wadi Dalfayn, about 45 km from Salut, and was discovered in 2009 by the French archaeological mission in central Oman led by Guillaume Gernez. The larger of two main buildings, about 15 m long and built of cut sandstone blocks and earth bricks, held five battle-axes, five daggers with crescent-shaped pommels, about fifty arrowheads, five complete bows averaging about 70 cm and two bronze quivers of about 35 cm, each with six arrows. Many weapons are full size, others are reduced models or miniatures, which suggests a ritual purpose; the second building held small bronze snakes and fragments of ceramic incense burners. The site dates to Iron Age II (900–600 BC) and may have been a meeting place with social, political or religious roles, or a staging post on the ancient road between Adam and Sinaw.
sites.sig: The first non-utilitarian weapon deposit known from the Arabian Peninsula, linked to Iron Age rituals on the desert edge of central Oman.
refs: Gernez, G., Jean, M. & Benoist, A. (2017). The discovery of a new Iron Age ritual complex in central Oman: recent excavations near Ādam. Proceedings of the Seminar for Arabian Studies 47, 101–117. https://www.archaeopresspublishing.com/ojs/index.php/PSAS/article/view/1222

Kuronuma, T., Miki, T., Tanabe, K. & Kondo, Y. (2023). Iron Age landscape in the Tanuf District, Ad-Dākhliyyah Governorate. The Journal of Oman Studies 24, Table 1. https://archaeopresspublishing.com/ojs/index.php/jos/article/download/3206/2748/20223
CNRS (2016). First non-utilitarian weapons found in the Arabian Peninsula. ScienceDaily, 10 March 2016. https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2016/03/160310080816.htm

sites.s: Mud-brick harat of a desert-edge oasis · birthplace of the founder of the Al Busaidi dynasty
sites.dr: Old quarters, some reportedly pre-Islamic in origin
sites.el: Harat al Busaid has about 120 old houses and six towers
sites.te: The oasis at the desert’s door
sites.se: At Adam, last oasis before the open desert, old mud-brick quarters with round towers once welcomed trading caravans
sites.sa: في آدم، آخر واحة قبل الصحراء المفتوحة، احتضنت حارات قديمة من الطين ذات أبراج دائرية قوافل التجارة
sites.desc: Adam is a fertile oasis wilayat in Ad Dakhiliyah, about 225 km from Muscat on the edge of the central desert, watered by aflaj and described as a former hub for trade caravans. Its old quarters include Harat bani Shaiban, with about 70 houses, three-storey circular towers and three mosques; Harat al Hawashim, circular in plan with two gates and two towers; and Harat al Busaid, one of the oldest, with about 120 houses and six defensive towers. The houses and mosques were built of clay, stone and plaster on stone foundations 1–2 m deep with juss mortar, and some quarters are reported to be pre-Islamic in origin. Harat al Busaid is described as the birthplace of Ahmad bin Said, founder of the Al Busaidi dynasty.
sites.sig: A well-preserved example of the fortified mud-brick quarters of Oman’s interior oases, tied to the origins of the Al Busaidi state.
disc: About 120 houses in Harat al Busaid
refs: Oman Observer. Home to a vibrant history. https://www.omanobserver.om/article/26073/Local/home-to-a-vibrant-history
Wikipedia. Adam, Oman. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adam,_Oman
sites.conf: Coordinates are the Wikipedia point for Adam town (22°23′N, 57°32′E), minute precision (≈1–2 km), not a point on a single quarter. Timeline is a broad estimate (no construction dates in the sources). About 14 km from Mudhmar East

sites.s: Fog-fed limestone desert plateau of central Oman · Key Biodiversity Area of about 26,700 km²
sites.se: On this vast stony plain, sea fog waters shrubs that feed gazelles, ibex, eagles and larks
sites.sa: في هذا السهل الحجري الشاسع يسقي ضباب البحر الشجيرات التي تقتات عليها الغزلان والوعول والعقبان والقنابر
sites.desc: Jiddat al-Harasis is a limestone plateau of sandy depressions, gravel plains, karst, dunes and escarpments covering about 26,742 km² of central Oman, recognised as a Key Biodiversity Area. Sea fog supports relatively good cover of low shrubs, ephemeral grasses and occasional acacias, and water seepages along the Al Huqf escarpment act as a refuge for animals. Recorded species include golden eagle, houbara bustard, crowned and spotted sandgrouse, Dunn’s lark, Arabian gazelle, Nubian ibex, Arabian wolf, caracal, reintroduced Arabian oryx and the endemic lizard Uromastyx thomasi, with several plants nearly restricted to the site. In 2015 Arabian gazelles on the surveyed plateau of the Al Wusta Wildlife Reserve numbered about 275, a density of 0.161 per km², well below earlier levels.
sites.sig: The core desert habitat of central Oman’s gazelles, ibex and desert birds, much wider than the fenced oryx reserve inside it.
sites.ex: KBA factsheet 8233; Al Jahdhami et al. (2017)

sites.s: Landlocked freshwater lagoon of the Sahil al Jazir · at least 121 bird species
sites.te: A freshwater pool beside the sea
sites.se: A small lagoon among the dunes of Al Wusta where ducks, terns and gulls rest and gazelles come to drink
sites.sa: بحيرة صغيرة بين كثبان الوسطى تستريح فيها البط والخطاطيف البحرية والنوارس، وتقصدها الغزلان
sites.desc: Khawr Dhirif is a landlocked, mostly freshwater lagoon of about 900 × 600 m on the Sahil al Jazir coastal plain of Al Wusta, recognised as a Key Biodiversity Area of about 0.98 km². It is surrounded by flat sandy terrain and dunes, with salt-tolerant shrubs near the water and aquatic Potamogeton and Ruppia. At least 121 bird species have been recorded, including wintering and migrating ducks such as ferruginous duck (Aythya nyroca), gulls, and gull-billed, Caspian, greater crested and Sandwich terns; Arabian gazelles are regularly seen. The lagoon lies within the proposed North Jazir National Nature Reserve of 15,000 ha.
sites.sig: A rare freshwater stopover for waterbirds on the arid Al Wusta coast.
refs: KBA Partnership. Khor Dirif (KBA 8235). Key Biodiversity Areas factsheet. https://www.keybiodiversityareas.org/site/factsheet/8235
sites.conf: Coordinates are the published KBA centre point (18.9333, 57.3500), about 1 km precision; t0 counts from the 1994 assessment. Arabic خور ذرف is a careful transliteration of the national name Khawr Dhirif. About 85 km from Khawr Ghawi
